 Malachi Toney passes Pro Football Hall of Famer on Miami career receiving yards list    
 By Alan Rubenstein 
  | 
 Last updated Oct 21, 2026 1:30 PM ET
 Add us as a preferred source on Google
 With 11 receptions for 154 yards and two touchdowns against Florida State on Saturday, Malachi Toney passed Pro Football Hall of Famer Andre Johnson  on the Miami career receiving yardage list. Toney is 11th in Miami history with 1,969 receiving yards after his big game in the Hurricanes' 43-35 double-overtime win over FSU.
 Toney is fifth in Miami history with 159 receptions and ninth with 18 career TD receptions. By the end of the 2026 regular season, Toney should own Miami's career records for receptions and receiving yards and have an outside chance at the TD record.
 Johnson is 31st in Miami history with 92 receptions, 14th with 1,831 yards and seventh with 20 TD receptions. Most of Johnson's production occurred in 2001 and 2002 after he played behind Santana Moss and Reggie Wayne as a freshman in 2000.
 Xavier Restrepo holds the Miami career records with 200 receptions and 2,844 receiving yards. Pro Football Hall of Famer Michael Irvin holds the Miami record with 26 career receiving TDs.
 Malachi Toney is chasing his own records
 While chasing the Miami career receiving records, Toney is also in position to break his own single-season records of 109 receptions and 1,211 receiving yards, set as a true freshman in 2025. Toney has 50 receptions for 758 yards and eight TDs in 2026. He set the Miami single-season records in 16 games in 2025.
 Leonard Hankerson set the Miami single-season record with 13 receiving TDs in 2013. At his current pace, Toney would break his own Miami single-season receiving yardage record on Nov. 7 at Notre Dame . Hankerson's single-season Miami TD reception record would be on pace to fall against Duke on Nov. 14.
 Toney breaking his own single-season reception record would depend on how far Miami advances in the postseason. Restrepo needed five seasons to break Miami's career reception and receiving yardage records. Toney should shatter those records in two years with Miami.
 Alan Rubenstein
